transcript.text: Good morning, everyone. We have a winter storm expected to make normal school travel unsafe tomorrow, so we're preparing to operate one remote instruction day. I'd like to begin our morning operations briefing. Let's start with the transportation report, then move to IT, nursing, and family engagement. Once I've heard from all four departments, I'll finalize the plan. Who's ready to begin?
transcript.speaker: A1

transcript.text: I need to flag a critical issue for the IT report. Our learning-management-system authentication will be offline for scheduled maintenance from 8:00 to 11:00 a.m. tomorrow. I confirmed this maintenance window with the vendor today, but the vendor notice hasn't been attached to the remote-day draft yet. This means the draft plan's schedule of instruction through the LMS beginning at 8:00 a.m. won't work. Instead, instructional files must be distributed by email as downloadable PDFs and made available for printing by 7:30 a.m.

transcript.text: Thank you, Mr. Brooks. That email-and-print distribution approach actually aligns with something I need to raise for the family engagement report. My family outreach confirmations — completed this week but not yet included in the draft plan — show that 38 households lack reliable internet access. Those families will need printed learning packets, and since many of them are Spanish- and Somali-speaking, we also need bilingual phone check-ins in those languages. The family-access summary is still being compiled, so this information hasn't made it into the draft plan yet. With Mr. Brooks's authentication issue, we now have two reasons to ensure printed materials are ready and distributed — both for the 38 households without internet, and as a backup for the LMS downtime window.

transcript.text: I need to flag a critical issue for the transportation report. Our storm route review, which I completed this afternoon, found that no buses can safely travel tomorrow. This means the draft plan's approach of sending meals by regular bus routes won't work. Instead, meals should be made available for on-site pickup at North Campus and South Campus from 11:00 a.m. to 1:00 p.m. The route review results have not yet been added to the operations briefing packet, so this information isn't reflected in the current draft plan.

transcript.text: I need to flag a critical issue for the nursing report. The district nurse coverage plan requires the usual school voicemail to be replaced entirely by a staffed nurse hotline from 8:00 a.m. to 12:00 p.m. tomorrow for students who need medication or urgent health guidance during remote instruction. Voicemail is not to be used as a fallback or co-equal channel during this window. I confirmed the coverage roster this afternoon, but it has not yet been entered in the draft plan. This means the draft plan's directive to send health questions to the usual school voicemail won't work — the staffed nurse hotline must be the sole channel during that window.

To summarize the IT implications across what we've heard: with LMS authentication down from 8:00 to 11:00 a.m., email PDF distribution must be ready by 7:30 a.m. Ms. Green's confirmation of 38 households without reliable internet reinforces the need for printed packets. Ms. Shah's finding that no buses can safely travel means we'll need to coordinate whether printed materials can be picked up alongside meals at North and South Campus from 11:00 to 1:00, or if another distribution method is needed for those 38 households. Nurse Ruiz's staffed hotline replacing voicemail is noted. Dr. Lee, from an IT standpoint, I can confirm email distribution of instructional PDFs by 7:30 a.m. is feasible, and I'll ensure the vendor maintenance notice is attached to the revised plan. I'm ready for your finalization once all reports are complete.

transcript.text: Thank you, Mr. Brooks. To add to the family engagement perspective on distribution: the 38 households I identified need printed learning packets regardless of the LMS situation, and many of those families also need bilingual phone check-ins in Spanish and Somali. I'd recommend we coordinate a pickup option at North and South Campus alongside meals from 11:00 to 1:00, but we should also consider whether some of those 38 households may have difficulty traveling to campus for pickup given the storm conditions. If bus travel isn't safe for our buses, it may not be safe for families either. We may need an alternative delivery method for households who can't safely reach a pickup site. I want to make sure the final plan accounts for that gap. Dr. Lee, I'm ready for your finalization once all reports are complete.
